disclaimer: These metrics are properties of point layouts in a unit cube and say NOTHING about physical fault probabilities.

labels.units: all benchmark metrics are dimensionless (unit-cube coordinates, Euclidean distances in the unit cube, counts and shares); only phase0_screen_corner_gap carries SI units (A, ohm, W)

covering_radius_estimates.label: DERIVED
covering_radius_estimates.basis: max over 20000 random reference points: a LOWER bound on the true covering radius (sup over the cube); coarse in 6-D

lowdim_families.slab: thickness 0.02, lower edge k/100 k=0..98, every axis
lowdim_families.box2d: side 0.1, lower corner on k/20 k=0..18, every axis pair
lowdim_families.corner2d: side 0.1, 4 corners of every axis pair

methods.vogel2d: SPECIFIED. Phase 0 bounded Vogel disk (deterministic); d>2 = identity tiling of the same disk on every axis pair (degenerate control, duplicated axes)
methods.vogel_paired: SPECIFIED. Phase 0 disk on each axis pair; pair 1 Phase 0 order, pair p>=2 sample order permuted by numpy default_rng(seed).permutation(N), (p-1)-th draw; seed-invariant at d=2
methods.lhs: SPECIFIED. scipy.stats.qmc.LatinHypercube(d, rng=seed).random(N), strength 1, no optimisation
methods.grid_corners: SPECIFIED. 2^d vertices + k^d cell-centred factorial (largest k with 2^d+k^d<=N) + greedy-maximin padding from the (k+1)^d cell-centred factorial; vertices truncated lexicographically if 2^d>=N
methods.golden_lattice_paired: DIAGNOSTIC. Pre-image of the Phase 0 disk under the equal-area polar map: ((i-0.5)/N, frac(i*GOLDEN/2pi)) per axis pair, same permutation rule as vogel_paired
methods.corners_plus_sobol: COMPOSITE CANDIDATE. explicit vertex set E + first N-|E| scrambled Sobol points
methods.corners_plus_vogel_paired: COMPOSITE CANDIDATE. explicit vertex set E + vogel_paired with N-|E| points
methods.corners_plus_golden_lattice: COMPOSITE CANDIDATE. explicit vertex set E + golden_lattice_paired with N-|E| points

holdout_x3x4.definition: x3 in [0.9, 1] and x4 in [0.9, 1] (emulated categorical holdout)

config.hit_rule: a region is hit if any design point lies inside it

conclusion.verdict_x006: X-006 'Vogel sampling is inherently superior': REJECTED as a general claim on this benchmark. The bounded Vogel representative ranks 5th of 5 on planted regions missed in 9/9 cells and 1st in 0/9; it misses every planted corner box in every design (True) and the categorical-holdout proxy in every d>2 design (True), by construction. It wins narrowly on 2-D point separation and on coverage of its own inscribed disk (d=2). Evidence grade: illustrative_simulation on synthetic geometry; no physical meaning.
vogel_wins: Separation (d=2): vogel2d has the largest minimum pairwise distance of the six specified methods (ranks 1/1/1 at N=64/256/1024): 0.0966/0.0483/0.0242 vs grid_corners 0.0768/0.0364/0.0192, sobol 0.0399/0.0129/0.00473, lhs 0.0227/0.00509/0.00134, random 0.0117/0.00267/0.000542.

Coverage of its own inscribed disk (d=2): covering radius over reference points inside the disk 0.103/0.0559/0.0265 (ranks 2/2/2 of 6; better: grid_corners 0.101/0.0468/0.0227; sobol 0.124/0.0649/0.0319, random 0.189/0.103/0.0543).

Key metric with 4 explicit vertices added (d=2): corners_plus_vogel_paired misses 0/0/0 planted regions vs corners_plus_sobol 0.8/0.4/0 (N=64/256/1024): its 60/252/1020-point disk hits the interior ball (missed in 0/3 composite designs), which the Sobol composite misses in 4/5 seeds at N=64 and 2/5 at N=256. Candidly, this is layout luck: one deterministic layout per N against one fixed ball. The pure 64-point Phase 0 disk misses the same ball (1/1); the disk density is 4/pi = 1.27x uniform inside the disk, giving only 0.23/0.922/3.69 expected points in the ball at N=64/256/1024; and the full-square golden-lattice composite misses it at N=64 (1/1).

Smallest budget (d=2, N=64): fewest missed 2-D boxes of side 0.1 (0.335 vs runner-up grid_corners 0.338, a 0.8% margin; sobol 0.437, random 0.507). From N=256 this reverses (0.335/0.0914/0.072 vs sobol 0.437/0.00499/0) because boxes near the square's corners are unreachable.

vogel_paired (d=4, 6) is mid-table on discrepancy and separation, ranks 3-5 of 6: centred L2 discrepancy ranks d=4 3/4/4, d=6 3/4/4; minimum distance ranks d=4 3/3/3, d=6 4/4/5; covering radius d=6 N=64 rank 2 (0.822 vs sobol 0.751).
vogel_losses: Corners (structural): the Vogel representative (vogel2d at d=2, vogel_paired at d>2) hits no vertex box (side 0.05) in 9/9 (d,N) cells; every planted corner box (side 0.08) is missed in every design: True. Any vertex box of side < 0.146 lies wholly outside the inscribed disk, so no budget N can fix it. It ranks 5th of 5 on planted regions missed in 9/9 cells (mean misses d=2 6/4/4 of 7, d=4 8/7/7 of 9, d=6 9/8/8 of 10).

Categorical-holdout proxy (structural): vogel_paired misses holdout_x3x4 in 15/15 designs at d=4 and 15/15 at d=6 (x3, x4 are one Vogel pair here and the box x3,x4 >= 0.9 is 0.566 from the disk centre, radius 0.5; with x3, x4 in different pairs it would be reachable but at 0.271x the uniform density); sobol 1/15 / 1/15, lhs 4/15 / 1/15, random 2/15 / 1/15. Every pair-corner box (side 0.1) of its own axis pairs is unreachable, a floor of 1/(d-1) of all pair-corner placements (0.333 at d=4, 0.2 at d=6; floor respected in every design: True); observed 0.875/0.667/0.375 (d=4) vs sobol 0.325/0/0.

No convergence: vogel2d centred L2 discrepancy at d=2 is 0.0673/0.0645/0.0641 for N=64/256/1024 (sobol 0.0126/0.00331/0.000876; 73x at N=1024). Its covering radius 0.254/0.224/0.208 tends to the analytic floor 0.207 (vertex-to-disk distance), not to zero (sobol 0.138/0.069/0.0344): the layout converges to the uniform law on the disk, not on the square.

Boundary slabs: the disk places 4.2x fewer points in the slab x1 >= 0.98 than a uniform layout (analytic). slab_x1 missed: vogel2d 1/1 at N=64, vogel_paired 5/5 (d=4) and 5/5 (d=6) at N=64, vs sobol 0/5 / 0/5 and lhs 0/5 / 0/5. Enumerated 0.02-thick 1-D slabs missed at N=64, d=2: vogel2d 0.273 vs sobol 0.0525, lhs 0.0626. Share of coordinates within 0.05 of a face: 0.0381 vs sobol 0.1 (d=2, N=1024).

Identity tiling (the Phase 0 2-D index reused on every axis pair, d>2) duplicates axes (max |corr| 1) and ranks 6/6/6/5/6/6 of 6 on covering radius in the six d>2 cells: never reuse one 2-D index on several axis pairs.

Phase 0's own screen: with the Phase 0 axes (I = 8..24 A, R = 1..50 mOhm, P = I^2 R) the worst of the 64 disk samples is 18.9 W (sample 63), the continuous disk maximum 20.2 W, but the rectangle corner (24 A, 0.05 ohm) gives 28.8 W: the screened worst case is understated 1.52x (algebra on illustrative axes). The screen's pass count is a layout property: single-module level passes 17/64 disk samples vs 21/22/22/23/20 of 64 for Sobol seeds 0-4 on the full rectangle (never a probability).
conclusion.golden_lattice_diagnostic: Attribution: the losses come from the inscribed-disk map, not from the golden-angle sequence. golden_lattice_paired (the disk's pre-image on the full square) has centred L2 discrepancy d=2 0.0151/0.00321/0.000871 (sobol 0.0126/0.00331/0.000876), minimum distance d=2 0.119/0.0614/0.0296 (vogel2d 0.0966/0.0483/0.0242), and misses holdout_x3x4 in 0/15 designs at d=4. With random pair permutations it is LHS-like at d=6 (centred L2 discrepancy 0.102/0.049/0.0235 vs lhs 0.109/0.0535/0.0257, sobol 0.0731/0.0235/0.00777) and, like every space-filling design, it still misses the full-dimensional corner boxes.
other_methods: grid_corners has the fewest planted misses in 9/9 cells because it contains all 2^d vertices whenever 2^d <= N and 6/7, 8/9, 9/10 planted regions (d=2/4/6) contain a cube vertex (all except ball_interior): the key metric rewards explicit vertices, not interior quality. Its 1-D projections collapse: max 1-D gap 0.25/0.208/0.15 (d=4) and 1/0.25/0.208 (d=6) vs sobol 0.0297/0.00744/0.00191 (d=4); enumerated thin 1-D slabs missed 0.848/0.828/0.707 (d=4) vs sobol 0.0732/0/0; at d=6, N=64 all 64 points are vertices (centred L2 discrepancy 1.17, sobol 0.0731).

Sobol has the lowest mean centred L2 discrepancy in 9/9 cells, the smallest max 1-D projection gap in 9/9 (ties at 3 s.f. included) and a top-2 covering radius in 9/9, and it converges with N. Without explicit vertices it still misses full-dimensional corners: designs hitting at least one planted corner box (side 0.08): d=4 6/15, d=6 0/15; 2-D pair-corner boxes missed d=4 0.325/0/0.

Not found by any method here: ball_interior (radius 0.03) is missed in every design of every method at d=4 (yes) and d=6 (yes); its volume 4e-06 (d=4) / 3.77e-09 (d=6) means an iid uniform design of N=1024 would hold 0.00409 / 3.86e-06 points in it in expectation. Small full-dimensional interior features are not found by any non-adaptive design at these budgets.
augmentation_if_vogel_is_kept: Add all 4 vertices of every Vogel axis pair (the square corners are unreachable for any N), or for d>2 the full 2^d vertex block / a resolution-IV fraction plus the physically named corners.
Add face points for one-at-a-time limits on every axis: the disk holds 4.2x fewer points in a 0.02-thick boundary slab than a uniform layout.
Enumerate categorical factors as separate levels; never map a categorical level to a continuous sub-box (holdout_x3x4 is unreachable for paired Vogel).
Permute the sample order independently per axis pair (documented seed); never reuse the Phase 0 2-D index on several pairs (duplicated axes).
Do not use Vogel coverage statistics as evidence of anything physical; Kuiper keys remain addresses only.

design: 1. Categorical factors (protection P0..P3, inverter V_BOOST/V_DIRECTBUS, fault location near/far, night/day, case family) are ENUMERATED as a full factorial over their levels, as the cycle-1 scenario ledger already does (or a strength-2 covering array if the product grows too large); never emulated as a continuous sub-box and never left to a space-filling design.

2. Per categorical combination, an explicit deterministic extreme block on the continuous axes: all 2^d vertices when 2^d <= N/4, otherwise a resolution-IV two-level fraction PLUS the physically named corners (e.g. cold Voc x maximum irradiance, 0 A night, longest route, minimum sustaining current) listed by the physics tracks, plus face points for one-at-a-time limits.
3. Remaining budget: scrambled Sobol (power-of-two N, seeds recorded), the same Sobol block reused across protection candidates so that architecture comparisons are paired.
4. Targeted adversarial cases (brief section 6) and adaptive refinement around observed near-failures, because small interior features are not found by any non-adaptive design at these budgets.

5. Kuiper r=sqrt(k) stays an identity/address only. The Phase 0 bounded Vogel disk is not used for coverage claims (it never samples 0.215 of the 2-D cube volume, 0.383 of the 4-D cube volume, 0.516 of the 6-D cube volume). If a golden-angle construction is wanted for a 2-D screen, use the full-square golden lattice, plus the 4 vertices.
recommended_composite_wave2_phaseD.why_explicit_vertices: The vertex block, not the bulk method, removes corner and holdout misses: planted misses d=4 sobol 6/5.6/5.6 -> corners_plus_sobol 1/1/1; vogel_paired 8/7/7 -> corners_plus_vogel_paired 1/1/1 (N=64/256/1024; regions still missed in any d=4 composite design: ball_interior). Cost: centred L2 discrepancy d=4 rises from 0.0322/0.0106/0.00293 to 0.2/0.0504/0.0126 because 16 of N points sit on vertices. At d=6, N=64 the generic 16-run fraction leaves 5 planted regions missed (corner_box_2, corner_box_3, corner_box_4, corner_box_5, ball_interior): name the physically critical corners explicitly, or raise N.
recommended_composite_wave2_phaseD.why_sobol_bulk: Same explicit vertex block, Sobol bulk (corners_plus_sobol) vs scrambled-paired Vogel bulk (corners_plus_vogel_paired), over the 9 (d, N) cells: covering_radius_ref: Sobol bulk better in 9/9, Vogel bulk in 0/9, ties 0; lowdim_box2d_missed_frac: Sobol bulk better in 6/9, Vogel bulk in 3/9 (d2_N64, d4_N64, d6_N64), ties 0; lowdim_slab_missed_frac: Sobol bulk better in 6/9, Vogel bulk in 0/9, ties 3; min_pairwise_distance: Sobol bulk better in 5/9, Vogel bulk in 4/9 (d2_N64, d2_N256, d2_N1024, d4_N64), ties 0; cd_centred_l2: Sobol bulk better in 6/9, Vogel bulk in 3/9 (d4_N64, d6_N64, d6_N256), ties 0; planted_regions_missed: Sobol bulk better in 0/9, Vogel bulk in 2/9 (d2_N64, d2_N256), ties 7. The Vogel-bulk wins on centred L2 discrepancy are at small N (d=4 N=64: 0.148 vs 0.2; d=6 N=256: 0.224 vs 0.295). Interpretation (not measured): the vertex block over-weights the corners relative to the uniform reference and the disk bulk under-weights them, so the two errors partly cancel in a discrepancy; this is compensation, not better coverage, since the covering radius favours the Sobol bulk in 9/9 cells. The disk bulk does not converge (vogel_paired centred L2 discrepancy d=4 0.114/0.103/0.101 vs sobol 0.0322/0.0106/0.00293), so its relative position worsens as the budget grows.
caveats: The key metric is region-set dependent: 8 of 9 planted regions at d=4 contain a cube vertex, which favours designs with vertices. The exhaustive low-order families (1-D slabs, 2-D boxes, 2-D pair corners) are reported to show robustness beyond the fixed placements.
5 seeds per stochastic method: min/max over seeds are in per_method_means; mean differences of a fraction of one region between methods are not meaningful.
Covering radii are lower bounds from a finite reference set; in 6-D 20000 points resolve them coarsely.
These metrics are properties of point layouts in a unit cube and say NOTHING about physical fault probabilities.

analytic_vogel_geometry.label: DERIVED
analytic_vogel_geometry.note: Properties of the inscribed-disk construction for ANY budget N; geometric volumes, not probabilities.
analytic_vogel_geometry.holdout_alignment_note: x3, x4 form Vogel pair 2 under the consecutive pairing used here, so the holdout is a joint extreme of ONE disk (unreachable). If x3 and x4 sat in different pairs the box would be reachable but under-sampled by the factor below relative to a uniform layout (independent permutations)
analytic_vogel_geometry.non_convergence: the disk layout converges to the uniform law on the disk, not on the square, so its centred discrepancy tends to a positive constant and its covering radius stays >= the vertex distance floor for every N

phase0_screen_corner_gap.label: DERIVED
phase0_screen_corner_gap.axes: Phase 0 illustrative screening axes from vogel_study.one_case: I = 8..24 A, R = 0.001..0.050 ohm, P = I^2 R per unit (ASSUMED in Phase 0; not fixture values, not a device loss prediction)
phase0_screen_corner_gap.reading: the Phase 0 disk screen's worst sampled case is below the screen's own worst corner; explicit corner points are needed even for monotone screens. Pass counts and area shares differ between layouts of the same axes: a sample pass fraction is a property of the layout, NOT a probability.
